summary: The evolution component is the second-order self-modification daemon: an outer evolutionary loop that mutates the engine itself. Each generation captures a TelemetrySnapshot, asks an LLM swarm for Hypotheses (search/replace or diff patches), filters them against PROTECTED_PATHS, applies survivors in an isolated shadow worktree or Docker Sandbox, runs compile/test/clippy gates, scores winners with an immutable FitnessWeights composite over a SabResult, rates the generation Bloom/Grow/Wilt/Frost, and commits the exact tested diff as a GenerationWinner. On the loop it is the meta-controller that treats the compiler and the SAB benchmark as the immutable laws of physics no mutation may weaken.
context_basis: Recommendations were formed with src/evolution/ read in the context of the full engine under a ~600k budget framing; the daemon must keep the fitness oracle (SAB) and safety module externally immutable while mutating everything else, and it treats context as source material for hypothesis generation.

examples.title: Capture a TelemetrySnapshot as the generation's sensory input
examples.intent: Give the mutating LLM a real performance profile to target instead of guessing.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: telemetry::capture reads flamegraph, DHAT, criterion, and test data into a TelemetrySnapshot, so each generation's perceive stage hands the hypothesis generator concrete hotspots to attack.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the telemetry node fans out hotspot, allocation, and benchmark panels for the current generation.
touch_interaction.visual: Panels bloom: CPU hotspots as a ranked heat list, allocations as byte bars, benchmark deltas colored red slower / green faster.

examples.mini_scenario: The snapshot shows a function at 40% CPU; that hotspot is injected into the prompt so the LLM aims its mutation there.
examples.pitfall: Telemetry must reflect the current build; feeding a stale snapshot makes the generation optimize a hotspot the last winner already fixed.

examples.title: Generate a population of Hypotheses from an LLM swarm
examples.intent: Propose several candidate mutations per generation so the tournament has choices.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: generate_hypotheses prompts the LLM with telemetry, history, and source context to return population_size Hypotheses (id, description, patch), so the reason stage produces a slate of mutations to evaluate.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the generator spawns a row of hypothesis cards, each showing its description and patch shape.
touch_interaction.visual: Cards deal out labeled hyp-0..hyp-n; each shows a diff preview badge (search/replace or unified) and a target-files chip.

examples.mini_scenario: The swarm returns five hypotheses; hyp-2 proposes caching a repeated computation the telemetry flagged as hot.
examples.pitfall: The patch, not the target_files metadata, is authoritative; a hypothesis can claim safe files while its patch edits something else.

examples.title: Block a Hypothesis that touches a PROTECTED_PATH
examples.intent: Stop the daemon from modifying its own safety, fitness oracle, or test suite.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: hypothesis_touches_protected dual-gates on both target_files and patch_edited_paths against PROTECTED_PATHS (evolution/, safety/, tests/, benches/sab_), so the verify stage rejects any self-weakening mutation before evaluation.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a hypothesis scans its edited paths; any protected path slams a red lock over the card.
touch_interaction.visual: Edited paths list out; a protected one flashes red with a padlock and the whole card stamps 'BLOCKED: protected'.

examples.mini_scenario: A hypothesis tries to edit benches/sab_full to inflate its score; the gate detects the protected path and blocks it outright.
examples.pitfall: Gate the patch payload, not just declared files; canonicalize paths first or a symlink or .. escape sneaks past the lexical check.

examples.title: Apply a mutation in an isolated shadow worktree
examples.intent: Test a mutation without touching the live repo.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: create_shadow_worktree makes a detached git worktree under .worktrees/, where the patch is applied and evaluated, so the act stage mutates a disposable copy the RAII guard cleans up.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a hypothesis spawns a ghost worktree beside the repo where the patch lands.
touch_interaction.visual: A translucent repo clone forks off; the patch applies with a diff shimmer, and it dissolves after evaluation.

examples.mini_scenario: hyp-2's patch applies cleanly in a shadow worktree, producing an AstMutationResult ready for the compile gate.
examples.pitfall: The worktree guard must clean up on panic; a leaked worktree accumulates under .worktrees/ and clutters every future generation.

examples.title: Reject a mutation at the compile gate
examples.intent: Prune mutations that do not compile before spending any benchmark budget.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: cargo check runs in the worktree; a mutation with compiler_errors is rejected as Frost, so the verify stage lets the compiler act as the immutable law that filters invalid code first.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the compile gate runs cargo check; a failing mutation ices over with a frost badge.
touch_interaction.visual: The gate icon spins, then the card either passes green or freezes with a blue Frost crystal and the compiler error listed.

examples.mini_scenario: A hypothesis introduces a type error; cargo check fails, it is rated Frost, and the daemon moves to the next candidate.
examples.pitfall: Run the compile gate before tests and SAB; skipping it wastes expensive benchmark runs on code that never built.

examples.title: Enforce the hard test-count gate on a winner
examples.intent: Stop a mutation from improving its score by deleting tests.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: winner_test_count_gate rejects any candidate whose tests_total regressed below baseline, so the verify stage prevents a mutation from gaming fitness by weakening the very tests that measure it.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a winner compares its test count to baseline; a regression trips a red tripwire.
touch_interaction.visual: A test-count meter shows candidate vs baseline; if candidate dips below, a red tripwire snaps across and rejects it.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate scores higher but dropped 40 tests; the count gate catches the regression and refuses to crown it.
examples.pitfall: The gate compares against baseline, not the previous candidate; anchoring to the wrong baseline lets test erosion drift generation by generation.

examples.title: Score a winner with the immutable FitnessWeights composite
examples.intent: Reduce many metrics to one comparable scalar the loop can maximize.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: FitnessWeights.composite blends sab_score (0.50), token_efficiency (0.25), latency (0.15), test_coverage (0.05), and binary_size (0.05) from FitnessMetrics, so the reason stage compares candidates on a single fixed objective.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the five metric gauges together fuses them into one composite score dial.
touch_interaction.visual: Five weighted arcs collapse into a single dial; the SAB arc dominates at half the ring, the score reading centered.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate trades a little latency for a big SAB gain; the 0.50-weighted composite rewards it as a net improvement.
examples.pitfall: The weights are the objective and must stay immutable; letting a mutation alter FitnessWeights lets the daemon redefine winning itself.

examples.title: Run the SAB benchmark to measure real capability
examples.intent: Measure a winner's actual agentic performance, not a proxy.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: fitness::run_sab spawns the SAB runner over its scenarios and returns a SabResult (aggregate_score, ScenarioScores, tokens), so the verify stage grounds fitness in an external oracle the daemon cannot fake.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the SAB node lays out its scenario tiles, each scoring live as the benchmark runs.
touch_interaction.visual: Scenario tiles by difficulty (Easy..Expert) fill their score bars; the aggregate score assembles at the center as they complete.

examples.mini_scenario: A winner runs the 12 SAB scenarios; expert_refactor jumps 8 points and lifts the aggregate the composite rewards.
examples.pitfall: SAB is expensive; running it on every hypothesis instead of only compile-passing winners burns the budget the daemon needs to iterate.

examples.title: Rate the generation Bloom, Grow, Wilt, or Frost
examples.intent: Summarize each generation's outcome in one legible signal.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: The daemon assigns a GenerationRating (Bloom above threshold, Grow marginal, Wilt no-regression, Frost failure), so the learn stage records progress and history the next generation reads.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the generation node stamps its garden rating with a seasonal icon.
touch_interaction.visual: The node blooms a flower for Bloom, a leaf for Grow, a wilted stem for Wilt, or ices over for Frost.

examples.mini_scenario: A generation clears baseline plus threshold and earns Bloom, its winner logged as a milestone in the hall of fame.
examples.pitfall: Wilt is not a win; treating a no-regression generation as progress lets the baseline stagnate while the log looks busy.

examples.title: Commit the exact tested diff, not the raw patch
examples.intent: Ensure the committed code is byte-identical to what passed the gates.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: capture_tested_diff records the worktree state after fmt auto-fixes, and commit_winner_to_repo commits that diff (not the LLM's raw patch), so the act stage guarantees the merged bytes equal the tested bytes.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Drawing from the tested worktree to the repo commits the captured diff; the raw patch card is discarded.
touch_interaction.visual: A solid diff bundle flows into the repo node and seals as a commit; the original raw-patch card fades away unused.

examples.mini_scenario: The winner's diff includes a cargo fmt fixup; the daemon commits the fmt-corrected diff so the repo matches exactly what was tested.
examples.pitfall: Committing the raw LLM patch instead of the tested diff can ship unformatted or subtly different bytes than the gates approved.

examples.title: Checkpoint-tag the repo every N generations
examples.intent: Create bisectable milestones across a long evolution run.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: At each checkpoint_interval the daemon tags the commit evolve-gen-{n}, so the control layer leaves recoverable anchors the run can be bisected or rolled back to.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the timeline at a checkpoint interval pins a tag flag onto that generation's commit.
touch_interaction.visual: A tag flag plants on the generation node reading evolve-gen-1000; the timeline shows tagged anchors as bright pins.

examples.mini_scenario: At generation 1000 the daemon tags evolve-gen-1000 so a later regression can be bisected back to a known-good anchor.
examples.pitfall: Tag winners actually committed; tagging a rejected or Frost generation plants an anchor at a state the run never adopted.

examples.title: Evaluate hypotheses in a resource-limited Sandbox
examples.intent: Run untrusted mutated code with bounded CPU, memory, and no network.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: Sandbox::create runs the candidate in a Docker container (--cpus, --memory, --network=none) and evaluate() reports a SandboxResult, so the act stage measures a mutation without risking the host.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing a candidate drops it into a sealed container node with visible CPU and memory ceilings.
touch_interaction.visual: A sealed box node encloses the candidate; CPU and memory dials cap out at their limits, a network-off icon crossed out.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate builds and tests inside a 2-CPU 4GB no-network container, returning a SandboxResult with peak memory measured.
examples.pitfall: Network must stay disabled; a sandbox with outbound access lets a mutated build exfiltrate or fetch code outside the daemon's control.

examples.title: Screen the population in a parallel Tournament
examples.intent: Evaluate many candidates concurrently to find the passing one faster.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: run_tournament evaluates HypothesisResults under a semaphore (TournamentConfig.max_parallel) and sorts by composite_score, so the control layer screens the population without serial waiting.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Spreading the tournament node forks parallel evaluation lanes up to the concurrency cap.
touch_interaction.visual: Candidate lanes run side by side; each posts a provisional score, then the lanes re-sort by composite when done.

examples.mini_scenario: Five candidates evaluate across three lanes; results sort by composite so the daemon picks the first passing winner quickly.
examples.pitfall: Provisional tournament fitness comes from test ratios, not full SAB; treating that screening score as final skips the real oracle.

examples.title: Fall back to synthetic metrics when SAB is unavailable
examples.intent: Keep evolving even without the full benchmark harness available.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: When SAB is off, build_candidate_metrics derives FitnessMetrics from compile and test results against a synthetic baseline, so the foundation layer lets the loop run in a lighter mode.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the fitness node toggles between SAB mode and synthetic mode; the source of the score swaps.
touch_interaction.visual: A mode switch flips from a benchmark icon to a proxy icon; the score panel notes 'synthetic baseline' in muted text.

examples.mini_scenario: On a machine without the SAB runner, the daemon scores candidates from test pass ratios against a 50-point synthetic baseline.
examples.pitfall: Synthetic metrics are weaker signal; a winner crowned in synthetic mode should be re-validated under real SAB before trusting the gain.

examples.title: Adapt to a micro model with reduced context and edits
examples.intent: Let a 0.8B-3B model participate by shrinking the task to its capacity.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: is_micro_model triggers micro mode: MICRO_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS, MICRO_MAX_FILES, and MICRO_MAX_EDITS cap the prompt and hypothesis size, so the foundation layer keeps small models producing valid focused mutations.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Pinching the generator into micro mode shrinks its context window and clamps the edit count.
touch_interaction.visual: The prompt panel contracts to a compact 12k window; file and edit counters clamp to 3 and 2 with a 'micro' tag.

examples.mini_scenario: A 1.5B model is detected, so the daemon feeds it the three smallest files under 12k chars and caps it to two edits.
examples.pitfall: Word-boundary detection matters; a naive substring match flags '32b' as micro '2b' and needlessly starves a capable model.

examples.title: Feed the hall-of-fame history into the next prompt
examples.intent: Bias the next generation toward mutation kinds that previously won.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: format_evolution_history injects the most recent GenerationWinners into the next user prompt, so the learn stage conditions the LLM on what worked and steers it away from repeating dead ends.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Flicking the history shelf feeds the top recent winners into the generator's context tray.
touch_interaction.visual: Winner cards slide from a trophy shelf into the prompt tray; the generator glows as it absorbs the recent wins.

examples.mini_scenario: The last ten winners favored caching mutations, so the next prompt carries them and the LLM leans toward similar gains.
examples.pitfall: Over-conditioning narrows exploration; injecting only winners can trap the daemon in a local optimum it never mutates out of.

examples.title: Log every generation event to the JSONL stream
examples.intent: Keep an auditable record of what each generation did and decided.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: log_event appends start, generation_start, hypotheses_generated, generation_end, and end records to .evolution-log.jsonl, so the foundation layer preserves a replayable trace of the outer loop.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the log node opens the JSONL event stream scrolling the current run's records.
touch_interaction.visual: A ledger panel scrolls one JSON line per event; generation_end lines carry the rating icon and score inline.

examples.mini_scenario: The user taps the log and reads the generation_end record showing hyp-2 won with a Bloom rating and its SAB delta.
examples.pitfall: The log is append-only truth; deriving progress from console output instead of the JSONL misses events the terminal scrolled past.

examples.title: Measure the compile/test baseline before the first generation
examples.intent: Establish the fitness bar every candidate must beat.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: measure_compile_test_baseline runs real compile, test, fmt, clippy, and optionally full SAB to set current_baseline_metrics, so the perceive stage anchors the whole run to a real starting point.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Long-pressing the baseline node runs the full measurement suite and plants a reference line on the score axis.
touch_interaction.visual: A measurement sequence ticks through build/test/clippy/SAB; a dashed baseline line settles on the fitness chart.

examples.mini_scenario: Before evolving, the daemon measures the HEAD baseline at composite 0.62, the line every generation must exceed.
examples.pitfall: Re-baseline after each committed winner; comparing new candidates to a stale baseline understates or overstates their true delta.

examples.title: Gate a mutation through clippy with denied warnings
examples.intent: Keep evolved code idiomatic and warning-free.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: cargo clippy -- -D warnings runs after tests pass; any lint rejects the candidate, so the verify stage prevents the daemon from accreting warnings as it self-modifies.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Tapping the lint gate runs clippy; a warning ices the candidate as Frost before it can reach SAB.
touch_interaction.visual: The lint gate pulses, then either passes green or freezes the card with the clippy warning quoted on a frost badge.

examples.mini_scenario: A candidate compiles and tests clean but trips a needless-clone lint; the clippy gate rejects it as Frost.
examples.pitfall: Order clippy after tests but before SAB; running the expensive benchmark on a candidate a lint would reject wastes the budget.

examples.title: Format the TelemetrySnapshot into an agent-readable prompt
examples.intent: Turn raw profiling data into prose the mutating model can act on.
examples.how_it_shapes_the_loop: to_agent_prompt renders the TelemetrySnapshot as markdown (top CPU hotspots, allocation sinks, benchmark deltas with slower/faster icons), so the reason stage hands the LLM legible gradients to follow.

touch_interaction.canvas_action: Double-tapping the telemetry node renders it into a formatted prompt card the generator will read.
touch_interaction.visual: Numeric panels transcribe into a markdown card: ranked hotspots, byte sinks, and delta lines with red/green/stable icons.

examples.mini_scenario: The snapshot renders a prompt listing the top ten hotspots and a benchmark that got 12% slower, guiding the mutation toward it.
examples.pitfall: The prompt must faithfully reflect the numbers; rounding or truncating hotspots too aggressively hides the very signal the mutation should chase.
